sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry

announcements.name: Foundry now supports customizing agents with any open source framework or model
announcements.shortDescription: Beyond creating and deploying agents, Foundry enables fine-tuning open source models to reach production-quality bars.
announcements.longDescription: Foundry now enables not only creating and deploying agents but also customizing them using any open source framework and any open source model to reach production-quality bars. The speaker frames evals as test-driven development for agents, defining quality bars upfront so teams can swap between frontier models (like GPT 5.2) and small open source models while verifying quality. The demo uses a customer service retail agent with four custom tools, comparing GPT 5.2 against an open source model (Qwen 3 14B [inferred]).

announcements.name: Automatic trace capture and observability
announcements.shortDescription: Every session and interaction is automatically captured, including cost and reproducibility data, viewable at the level of individual session traces.
announcements.longDescription: Foundry recently launched the ability to dig into how models and agents work together by inspecting specific traces. Every single session and interaction with users is automatically captured, providing observability that includes reproducibility (to learn how the agent behaved) and cost, all captured automatically. Users can drill into traces of any specific session to see model invocations and tool calls such as order lookups and policy validation.

announcements.name: Converting production traces into training datasets
announcements.shortDescription: Traces from models and agents in production can be automatically converted into datasets for subsequent reinforcement learning runs.
announcements.longDescription: Traces from models and agents running in production can be automatically converted into datasets used for subsequent reinforcement learning to improve behavior over time. Users can select sessions executed against any model version to generate a training dataset, then choose which traces are useful and invoke subsequent reinforcement fine-tuning runs. This supports post-training, a broad umbrella term covering custom data, agent traces, distilled data from larger models, or synthetically generated data.

announcements.name: Native Ray dashboard integration and a rollout browser
announcements.shortDescription: Foundry offers an AAD-authenticated endpoint to manage an entire Ray cluster (CPU and GPU nodes), monitor jobs, and inspect RFT trajectories and rollouts.
announcements.longDescription: When kicking off a job, Foundry provides native integration with Ray dashboards and a rollout browser. Through an AAD-authenticated endpoint, users can manage an entire Ray cluster—including CPU nodes, GPU nodes, and everything in between—bring custom code and models, run GRPO, and monitor jobs and rollouts. The trajectories view in RFT lets users watch reinforcement fine-tuning in action, inspecting every sample's tool calls and how each call is rewarded toward the reward target.
